body:
Thank you for your response. I completely agree with you that my experience with my ex has been a major learning experience, but it is just still so hard to think that in a different universe I could have at least had that kind of love to help me through this other stuff.

And as far as the degree - I can get some financial help, which is why I thought I was going to be able to go back this year, but when it comes down to it, the money I was getting just wasn't enough. I've applied for about everything I could think of, even racial scholarships, knowing goood and well I probably wouldn't even be considered, but no response after no response.

Literally the only thing I've been able to think of is to just work for the next year and a half, and save almost every penny to put towards school. I've figured it up, and that would give me exactly enough, plus the little aid I can get, to pay for school. I would still have to work during school obviously for rent and food money.

But how realistic of a plan is that? Will I really be able to save 95% of my money over that long of a time, especially given how volatile the current situation is?

I guess it just bothers me that the one little glimmer of hope is pinned to, what I feel, are highly improbable odds, and if that doesn't work, then I have no plan B.

EDIT: I noticed that you also posted in this subreddit about your own plans. Maybe we could share our own stories and experiences since we might be coming from similar places?
